goals: Quantify peak SWE variation across the Wenatchee elevation gradient (187-2870 m)
Validate model peak SWE against 5 SNOTEL stations
key_processes: Snow accumulation and melt timing as functions of elevation/temperature

model_choice.rationale: ELM simulates snow accumulation/melt and outputs SWE variables (H2OSNO). NLDAS-2 forcing provides elevation-resolved precipitation across the basin's 2683 m relief. Single-column mode is appropriate—SWE is a local vertical process without lateral transport.

answerable: Elevation control on peak SWE via orographic precipitation gradient (NLDAS-2 resolves ~12 km terrain, verified to span ~15 precip values across similar relief)
Co-located validation against 5 SNOTEL stations (H2OSNO output is available, peak-SWE comparison is explicitly supported)

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by elevation with validation pinning
sampling_strategy.n_justification: Three elevation bands × 3 replicates per band = 9 exploratory columns. This minimal design resolves the single driver (elevation) with light replication to assess within-band variability and NLDAS cell-to-cell differences. Total N=14 (9 exploratory + 5 validation) is defensible for a one-gradient question.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate 4-5 columns in the rain-snow transition (1000-1500 m) where SWE is most sensitive to elevation/temperature. Ensure 3-4 columns above 2000 m where SNOTEL stations cluster. Avoid extreme low elevations (<500 m) where snow is ephemeral. Within bands, sample across the basin's longitudinal extent to capture NLDAS cell diversity.
sampling_strategy.replication: 3 columns per elevation band to assess within-band variability and provide robustness against individual NLDAS cell artifacts.

sampling_plan.reason: Pinned to 5 SNOTEL locations for co-located peak SWE validation—non-negotiable, dictated by data availability.
Captures elevation zone where precipitation partitioning shifts from rain-dominated to snow-dominated—highest SWE sensitivity.
Represents consistent winter snowpack zone—tests model's accumulation/melt timing in the core snow regime.
Captures deep, long-lasting snowpack where SNOTEL stations concentrate—tests model at upper elevation extreme.

validation_design.comparison: co-located: model H2OSNO annual maximum at SNOTEL coordinates vs observed peak SWE
validation_design.metric: bias (model - obs), RMSE, and Pearson correlation across 5 stations to assess elevation-gradient skill

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (2009-2018, 10 years), native SSURGO soil at each location, default ELM snow physics

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL station metadata (coordinates, elevations) for the 5 in-domain stations
requires_capabilities.why: Needed to pin validation columns to exact SNOTEL locations and retrieve observed peak SWE time series
requires_capabilities.blocks: Co-located validation—without coordinates, we cannot place columns or compare

requires_capabilities.capability: Peak SWE extraction from H2OSNO time series (annual maximum)
requires_capabilities.why: Validation metric requires identifying the single maximum SWE value per water year from model output
requires_capabilities.blocks: Validation comparison—raw H2OSNO is daily/subdaily; peak SWE is a derived metric

requires_capabilities.capability: Sub-12 km terrain downscaling for NLDAS forcing (future enhancement, not required)
requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS 12 km cells average over terrain—ridgetop SNOTEL stations may see underestimated precipitation. Finer-scale downscaling (e.g., lapse-rate adjustment within cells) would improve ridgetop skill.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Nothing—experiment is feasible without this, but it would reduce known ridgetop bias

assumptions: The 5 SNOTEL stations span the basin's elevation range adequately (if all cluster at high elevations, validation of low-elevation model behavior is limited)
NLDAS-2 orographic precipitation gradient is sufficient to resolve elevation control on SWE (verified for similar relief, but Wenatchee-specific validation is pending)
10-year simulation period (2009-2018) captures representative interannual snowpack variability
Default ELM snow physics (no tuning) is appropriate—validation will reveal any systematic biases
SNOTEL peak SWE observations are quality-controlled and representative of their local ~100 m footprint (model represents ~12 km cell average)
open_questions: Do the 5 SNOTEL stations span low/mid/high elevations, or do they cluster (e.g., all >1800 m)? This affects validation coverage.
Are SNOTEL peak SWE data available for the full 2009-2018 period, or are there gaps?
Should we include a sensitivity test (e.g., ±10% precipitation perturbation) to quantify SWE response, or is the elevation gradient alone sufficient?
